items.headline: Three Malaysians charged after collecting S$200,000 for a scam syndicate
items.summary: Three Malaysian men aged 22 to 24 were charged on June 20 after entering Singapore on June 18 to collect cash and gold for a Malaysia-based scam syndicate; police recovered 69 bank cards used to withdraw about S$200,000.

items.headline: Singapore electricity tariff set to rise from July as gas prices climb
items.summary: The Energy Market Authority signalled the regulated electricity tariff is likely to rise from July on higher natural-gas prices, after a 2.1% increase in the April-to-June quarter; U-Save rebates are due in July.

items.headline: HDB launches 6,952 BTO flats including the first ever in Lakeview
items.summary: HDB launched 6,952 flats on June 17 across seven projects, including Lakeview Cascadia (1,221 units), the first Build-To-Order project in the new Lakeview estate; applications run until June 24.

items.headline: Counterfeit Sanrio seller fined S$13,000 as director jailed eight months
items.summary: Gem Story Biz was fined S$13,000 and its director Tan Mei Qin, 51, jailed eight months for selling more than 2,000 counterfeit Sanrio products; 14 of 75 Trade Marks Act charges were proceeded with.

items.headline: Operation Sindhu evacuates over 4,400 Indians from Iran and Israel
items.summary: India brought home 4,415 nationals (3,597 from Iran, 818 from Israel) on 19 special flights, including three IAF C-17s, under Operation Sindhu; Iran reopened its airspace on June 20 for flights via Mashhad.

items.headline: Modi leads the 12th International Yoga Day at Kolkata's Red Road
items.summary: PM Narendra Modi led the 12th International Day of Yoga on June 21 at Kolkata's Red Road under the theme 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing', joined by thousands and West Bengal Governor C V Ananda Bose.

items.headline: Railway worker killed as Avadh Assam Express hits a trolley in Bihar
items.summary: A trolleyman was killed and several track workers injured when the Dibrugarh-bound Avadh Assam Express struck a maintenance trolley near Katihar in Bihar on June 20; a high-level inquiry was ordered.

items.headline: Update: IMD forecasts very heavy rain over northeast India as monsoon nears Delhi
items.summary: The IMD forecast very heavy to extremely heavy rain over northeast India through June 25 and said the southwest monsoon is likely to reach Delhi between June 25 and 30 as heat lingered over the northern plains.

items.headline: Update: Starmer pressed to set a departure date as Burnham enters the Commons
items.summary: Pressure intensified on PM Keir Starmer to set out a timetable for his departure as Andy Burnham, who won the Makerfield by-election with 54.8%, was sworn into the Commons on June 22; Starmer held weekend talks at Chequers but vowed to stay.

items.headline: Met Office issues an amber extreme-heat warning as June record is threatened
items.summary: The Met Office issued an amber extreme-heat warning for much of England and Wales from June 22, with highs near 34C on Monday peaking around 38C by Wednesday and Thursday; the June record of 35.6C set in 1976 is likely to be broken.

items.headline: Farage breached MPs' rules 17 times over £384,000 in unregistered interests
items.summary: The Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards found Reform UK leader Nigel Farage breached the rules 17 times by failing to register about £384,000 of financial interests within 28 days, but ruled the breaches inadvertent and recommended no sanction.

items.headline: Tribunal finds an NHS trust discriminated against eight nurses over a changing room
items.summary: An employment tribunal ruled County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust harassed and discriminated against eight nurses by requiring them to share a changing room with a transgender colleague and failing to address their concerns.

items.headline: Russian-occupied Crimea halts civilian fuel sales after Ukrainian strikes
items.summary: Crimea governor Sergei Aksyonov suspended petrol sales to civilians from June 21, reserving fuel for security services, after overnight Ukrainian drone strikes on oil depots killed four and wounded 28; Kyiv said it hit depots in Kerch and Krasnodar.

items.headline: Colombia votes in a knife-edge runoff between de la Espriella and Cepeda
items.summary: Colombians voted June 21 in a polarising presidential runoff between Trump-backed conservative Abelardo de la Espriella (43.7% in round one) and leftist senator Iván Cepeda (40.9%); counting was under way in a contest set to redefine US ties.

items.headline: Poland strips Zelensky of its top honour in a WWII-era history dispute
items.summary: Polish President Karol Nawrocki revoked Zelensky's Order of the White Eagle after Ukraine renamed an army unit after the UPA; Zelensky returned the medal on June 20 and Kyiv's foreign minister called the move a strategic error that benefits Moscow.

items.headline: Zimbabwe parliament passes a bill scrapping direct presidential elections
items.summary: Zimbabwe's National Assembly passed Constitutional Amendment Bill No. 3 on June 19 by 216 votes to 42, replacing direct presidential elections with a parliamentary vote and extending terms from five to seven years; Tendai Biti called it a slow coup.

items.headline: Spain thrash Saudi Arabia 4-0 as Yamal and Oyarzabal star at the World Cup
items.summary: Spain beat Saudi Arabia 4-0 in Atlanta on June 21, with Lamine Yamal opening the scoring in the 10th minute and Mikel Oyarzabal scoring twice, to take command of their World Cup group.

items.headline: Pacific Fusion's Series A tops $1 billion, the largest in the fusion sector
items.summary: Pacific Fusion told TechCrunch its Series A has grown beyond $1 billion, paid in milestone-based tranches, which it describes as the largest early-stage round in the fusion-energy sector, backing its pulsed-magnetic approach.

items.headline: Qualcomm in talks to buy Jim Keller's Tenstorrent for up to $10 billion
items.summary: Qualcomm is in advanced talks to acquire RISC-V AI-chip start-up Tenstorrent, founded by Jim Keller, at a valuation of $8 billion to $10 billion, per The Information, in a bet on inference chips that challenge Nvidia.

items.headline: SpaceX agrees a $60 billion takeover of AI coding startup Cursor
items.summary: SpaceX has agreed to take over Anysphere, maker of the AI coding tool Cursor, at a valuation of about $60 billion, Bloomberg reported, days after SpaceX's record Nasdaq debut; the deal is expected to close later in 2026.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly prepares a confidential IPO filing at a $730 billion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly preparing to file confidentially for an IPO, with a listing possible later in 2026, after being valued at about $730 billion in private markets; it has recently strengthened its research leadership.

items.headline: Wall Street reopens after Juneteenth to a data-heavy week and a hawkish Fed
items.summary: US markets, shut June 19 for Juneteenth, reopen June 22 to flash PMIs, the final Q1 GDP reading and the May inflation gauge; the Fed's June projections showed nine of 18 officials expecting at least one 2026 rate increase.

items.headline: Oil holds near $80 as US-Iran talks in Geneva are abruptly postponed
items.summary: Brent crude held around $80.57 a barrel and WTI near $77.54 after US-Iran talks scheduled in Switzerland were abruptly postponed and VP JD Vance cancelled his trip, keeping a risk premium in the market.

items.headline: Update: SpaceX shares swing after a record IPO week as leveraged ETFs pile in
items.summary: After closing its first full week 37% above its $135 IPO price, SpaceX (SPCX) touched a high of $225.64 on June 16 before easing back toward $185 by June 21; at least 11 leveraged ETFs have launched to trade the stock.

items.headline: Tiafoe beats Fritz to win his first grass title at the Halle Open
items.summary: Frances Tiafoe beat fellow American Taylor Fritz 6-4, 6-4 in the Halle Open final on June 21 for the biggest title of his career and his first on grass, without facing a break point.

items.headline: Noskova beats Pegula in the Berlin final to close on the top 10
items.summary: Linda Noskova beat defending champion Jessica Pegula 6-4, 4-6, 6-3 in the rain-delayed Berlin Open final on June 21 for her second career title and first on grass, putting her on the verge of a top-10 debut.

items.headline: Cerundolo beats Paul for his first ATP 500 title at Queen's Club
items.summary: Francisco Cerundolo beat Tommy Paul in the Queen's Club final on June 21 to claim the biggest title of his career, his first at ATP 500 level, capping a strong grass-court run ahead of Wimbledon.

items.headline: South Africa beat India by six wickets at the Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: South Africa beat India by six wickets in Manchester on June 21, with Marizanne Kapp unbeaten on 81 from 45 balls to chase down 159 with balls to spare; it was India's first defeat of the tournament.

items.headline: Antonelli leads the F1 title race as the Austrian Grand Prix looms
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 drivers' championship on 156 points, 41 clear of Lewis Hamilton, who took his first Ferrari win at the Spanish Grand Prix in Barcelona; the next round is the Austrian GP at the Red Bull Ring on June 28.

items.headline: JUNO neutrino observatory delivers a landmark first precision measurement
items.summary: China's Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory published its first result, one of the most precise measurements yet of neutrino oscillation parameters, cutting the uncertainty by about 1.6x from 59 days of data.

items.headline: Webb measures a black hole that formed before its own galaxy
items.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope made the first direct mass measurement of an early-universe black hole, a 50-million-solar-mass object seen 700 million years after the Big Bang that appears to have outgrown its host galaxy.

items.headline: Ancient DNA shows plague was killing humans 5,500 years ago
items.summary: Ancient DNA from hunter-gatherer cemeteries near Lake Baikal in Siberia found early plague strains in nearly 40% of individuals studied, evidence of lethal outbreaks 5,500 years ago, pushing back the earliest known epidemics.

items.headline: Study finds developing neurons break their own DNA to build the brain
items.summary: Researchers reported in Nature that newborn neurons squeezing through tight spaces in the developing brain routinely suffer DNA double-strand breaks that are then repaired, a normal part of building the cerebral cortex.

fun_fact.headline: Flamingos get their pink colour entirely from their diet
fun_fact.body: Flamingos are not born pink. Their feathers start out grey, and the birds get their famous pink-and-orange colour entirely from their diet - pigments called carotenoids in the algae and brine shrimp they eat. A flamingo raised without those pigments in its food would simply stay white.

puzzle.title: Two Candles
puzzle.body: Two candles are the same length but different thicknesses. The thinner one burns down completely in 6 hours; the thicker one burns down completely in 4 hours. Both are lit at the same instant. After how long is one candle exactly twice as long as the other?
puzzle.approach: Track each candle's remaining length as a fraction of the time elapsed, then set one length equal to twice the other.
puzzle.answer: Three hours. With full length 1, the 6-hour candle has (1 - t/6) left and the 4-hour candle has (1 - t/4) left. Setting the slower candle to twice the faster: 1 - t/6 = 2(1 - t/4), giving t/3 = 1, so t = 3. At 3 hours the lengths are 1/2 and 1/4 - exactly twice.

word_puzzle.title: Tack It On
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into four groups of four; in each group every word becomes a compound word when the SAME word is added to its end. Words: STRAW, RASP, GOOSE, BLUE, KEY, CARD, DASH, BLACK, BUTTER, DRAGON, HORSE, FIRE, FOOT, FINGER, NEWS, THUMB.
word_puzzle.approach: Each word becomes a compound when the same second word is tacked onto its end; find the four shared endings.
word_puzzle.answer: +BERRY: STRAW, RASP, GOOSE, BLUE. +BOARD: KEY, CARD, DASH, BLACK. +FLY: BUTTER, DRAGON, HORSE, FIRE. +PRINT: FOOT, FINGER, NEWS, THUMB. Traps: BLACK fits blackberry but BERRY is full, so it goes to BOARD; BLUE fits blueprint but PRINT is full, so it goes to BERRY.
